When you attack with that type of weapon and the weapon is {@itemProperty F||finesse} or ranged, you can use your choice of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

In addition, when you hit a creature with the chosen weapon, you can spend a craft slot to roll a number of additional weapon damage dice on the damage roll. The number of additional weapon damage dice is equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Weavebonder
entries: With a nuanced touch, you can manipulate even the smallest ebbs and flows of an item's magic.

items: When you make an Enchanting check with a skill with which you are proficient, you have advantage on the roll.
When you roll for a quirk's random element (such as damage type, skill, or creature type), you can roll the die twice and choose either result.
Each hour you spend enchanting an item counts as 3 hours towards the item's completion.

name: Well-Read
entries: You grew up with your nose buried in books. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Creature Lore
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can recall lore about a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself; you know one {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}, {@spell Resistance|XPHB}, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB}, or Trait of that creature. You decide when you use this ability.

entries.name: Font of Useful Knowledge
entries: When you roll a 1 on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you can reroll the die, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Rare Knowledge
entries: If you succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB}) check, you learn additional lore. The GM has final say on what you learn, if anything. The lore might consist of important details, amusing revelations, or even secret lore that has never been widely known. The more information you already know about the thing, the more precise and detailed the information you receive is. That information is accurate but might be couched in figurative language or poetry, as determined by the GM.

name: Well-Versed
entries: You know the sagas of your people and others and can use that knowledge to help you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Lore Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one musical instrument and one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Useful Knowledge
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}) check, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll. You can do this a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Wetland Explorer
entries: Your deep knowledge of the dangerous creatures that inhabit the world aid you in both fighting and tracking them. You gain the following benefits:

items: Select two creature types of your choice. Whenever you roll initiative at the start of a combat that has one or more hostile creatures of the chosen type, you can add your proficiency bonus to the roll. If a creature has magically altered its form to appear as another creature type, you don't gain this benefit.
You gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks involving one or more of the chosen creature types.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls made against a target of the chosen creature type.

name: Wild Lore
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Knowledge of the Land
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) checks.

entries.name: Provider
entries: You can use your knowledge of the land to find food and fresh water for yourself and up to 3 other people each day.

entries.name: Fly Speed
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

name: Winter Initiate
entries: You have learned some of the secrets and techniques of the Children of Winter druidic order. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Life from Death
entries: Whenever you take Necrotic damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} after you take the damage.

entries.name: Summon Decay
entries: When you conjure a creature with a spell or magical ability, you can choose for that creature to be Undead instead of its usual creature type.

entries.name: Understand Disease
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks to research, diagnose, and treat disease.

entries.name: Children of Winter Spells
entries: The secrets you've learned allow you to always have certain spells at the ready. When you have spell slots of a level specified in the Children of Winter Spells table, you thereafter have the spells listed for that level and lower prepared.

name: Witch Hunter
entries: You have honed and perfected your skills fighting against spellcasters, possibly from your background hunting mages as part of the Arcanist Inquisition. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Dodge Spells
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to avoid a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect. Make a Wisdom saving throw against the spellcaster's spell save DC. On a successful save, the creature must choose a new target or the spell is canceled. A canceled spell dissipates with no effect, and any resources used to cast it are wasted.

entries.name: Keep Your Enemies Close
entries: When you hit a target that can cast spells with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can reduce its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 15 feet until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Resist Curses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against all Shadowsteel curses, and also against spells with a duration of more than 10 minutes.

name: Wood-Craft
entries: You are familiar with the difficulties encountered when crossing wild lands, and with the ways of overcoming them. You can make an Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check in place of any Wisdom ({@skill Explore|TLotRR}) or Wisdom ({@skill Hunting|TLotRR}) check.

In addition, you can spend 1 hour and a craft slot to make an Intelligence ({@skill Nature}), Wisdom ({@skill Explore|TLotRR}), or Wisdom ({@skill Hunting|TLotRR}) check (your choice). The DC is determined by the terrain type the Company is currently traversing (as if a journey event was taking place there; see {@book Chapter 5|TLotRR|4|Event Resolution}). The check has disadvantage if it is autumn or winter. If you succeed, choose one of the following options:

items: Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 1 hour, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also leave behind no tracks or other traces of their passage for the duration.

Choose a number of creatures equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1), which can include yourself. For 8 hours, each of those creatures has a +5 bonus to its passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score. When you reach 5th level, the bonus increases to +10. If you obtain a magical success, the creatures also gain {@sense tremorsense|MM} out to a range of 60 feet for the duration.

You forage a number of pounds of food and gallons of water equal to your check result minus the terrain DC (minimum 1). The food lasts for 24 hours, or 48 hours when you reach 5th level. If you obtain a magical success, each pound of food foraged in this way also restores 1 hit point to the creature eating it during a short or long rest.

name: Woodwise
entries: You have lived your entire life in the gnarled, wooded areas of the world. You are adept at finding your way through even the most treacherous terrain. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in either the {@skill Survival} or {@skill Nature} skill.
You ignore difficult terrain.
You cannot become lost in natural surroundings except by magical means.
